title: Quantitative machine learning of protein interactions reveals the multiscale organization and molecular syntax of signaling networks
authors: Julia R. Rogers; Loren P. Cardani; Neel H. Shah; Mohammed AlQuraishi
one_liner_zh: 该文用统计力学建模和神经网络预测蛋白-肽段结合亲和力，构建信号网络定量图谱，虽非直接结构预测/采样，但以蛋白相互作用结构机制为核心，方法可迁移至蛋白结构计算。
abstract: Cells employ dense networks of transient protein–protein interactions mediated by modular peptide-binding domains and unstructured peptidic motifs for high-fidelity information processing. How these networks physically execute computations through protein interactions governed by complex intra- and intermolecular mechanisms remains indiscernible from current, sparse and non-quantitative, maps of the human interactome. Here, we introduce a quantitative statistical mechanical modeling (QSM) approach for machine learning domain–peptide affinities with experimental-level accuracy. Leveraging a new, principled algorithm for data harmonization and a biophysically informed neural network architecture, QSM learns to predict dissociation constants directly from amino acid sequences with calibrated confidence. We use QSM to construct the first quantitative drafts of human signaling networks and study these networks across three physical scales—recognition mechanisms of modular binding domains, combinatorial logic of multi-dentate proteins, and pathways inferred from de novo inference of protein interaction networks. We find that (i) modular domains, based on their binding preferences, selectivities, and strengths, fall into a limited number of biophysical equivalence groups, (ii) those domains, along with peptidic motifs, are “syntactically” combined within proteins to yield multivalent recognition mechanisms, and (iii) the organization of cellular function can be traced back to algorithmically detectable modules induced by domain-mediated interactions. In aggregate, these analyses instantiate a tractable roadmap towards a comprehensive, mechanistic, and simulatable articulation of the systems biology of signaling.
abstract_zh: 细胞利用由模块化肽结合结构域和非结构化肽基序介导的瞬时蛋白-蛋白相互作用密集网络，进行高保真信息处理。这些网络如何通过受复杂分子内和分子间机制调控的蛋白质相互作用物理地执行计算，目前仍无法从现有稀疏且非定量的人类互作组图谱中辨别。在此，我们引入一种定量统计力学建模（QSM）方法，用于以实验级精度机器学习结构域-肽亲和力。利用一种新的、有原则的数据协调算法和生物物理信息化的神经网络架构，QSM学习直接从氨基酸序列预测解离常数，并带有校准的置信度。我们使用QSM构建人类信号网络的首次定量草图，并在三个物理尺度上研究这些网络——模块化结合结构域的识别机制、多齿蛋白的组合逻辑，以及从头推断蛋白相互作用网络所推导的路径。我们发现：（i）模块化结构域，基于其结合偏好、选择性和强度，归入有限数量的生物物理等价组；（ii）这些结构域连同肽基序，在蛋白质内以“句法”方式组合，产生多价识别机制；（iii）细胞功能的组织可追溯至由结构域介导相互作用诱导的算法可检测模块。总体而言，这些分析为实现信号系统生物学的全面、机制性和可模拟化阐述提供了一条可行的路线图。
